models.inverse_notes: IC = T/(CPI*Tc) needs CPI*Tc != 0; CPI = T/(IC*Tc); Tc = T/(IC*CPI). Check: T=0.6,IC=1e9,CPI=1.2 gives Tc = 0.5e-9. Zero factors map back against nonnegativity guards as degenerate ideals. Algebraic only.
limitations: Single-processor program execution only; multiprocessor/parallel effects need the speedup-law records.
Zero IC/CPI/Tc factors are degenerate ideals (no work, no cycles, frozen clock), not operating points.
MIPS/GHz in isolation mislead across ISAs (source warns instruction complexity varies); compare with matched IC.
